summary: Daniel Han, the algorithms engineer behind Unsloth, presents findings on bugs in open source language models at the AI Engineer World's Fair. He recaps Gemma and Phi-3 fixes from a prior workshop including approximate GeLU activation, sliding window should be 2048 not 2047, and unfusing QKV matrices for LoRA tuning. He then covers 8 Llama 3 bugs. Double BOS tokens from apply_chat_template plus manual BOS addition lower inference accuracy; Unsloth removes them automatically. Untrained tokens (reserve 0-250, end-of-turn, header tokens) cause NaN gradients; the instruct template must not be used with the base model. Fix by setting untrained tokens to the mean of trained tokens with careful masking. Pad and EOS tokens being identical causes infinite generations since pad masking removes EOS from loss; Unsloth fixes this by selecting an untrained token as pad. Community contributions include CPU-only GGUF conversion due to float16 precision differences and llama.cpp warning about double BOS. Unsloth features include 2x faster finetuning, 70% less VRAM, 4x longer context via gradient offloading to system RAM (1-2% slower), and continued pre-training with 5-10x reduced learning rate for LM head and embed tokens. The Colab demo covers LoRA configuration with rank 16 (suggested 16-128, max equals model dimension), alpha set to rank times two for better results, all linear layers (QKV, down, up, gate) as target modules, and use_rslora for automatic rank/alpha. Data preparation shows Titanic CSV fine-tuning with column merging for Ollama's two-column limitation, customizable chat templates requiring two iterations due to dangling newlines, and Llama 3 chat template examples. Training methodology recommends batch size 2, gradient accumulation 4 (effective batch size 8), and learning rate 2e-4 or smaller. Saving now supports multiple GGUF files without the previous 10-minute wait, with automatic Ollama model file generation.

sections.title: Introduction and Gemma/Phi-3 Recap
sections.summary: Daniel introduces himself from Unsloth, links to workshop slides, and recaps prior Gemma and Phi-3 fixes including approximate GeLU activation, sliding window should be 2048 not 2047, and unfusing QKV matrices for LoRA tuning. He announces 8 Llama 3 bugs to be covered.

sections.title: Llama 3 Bug 1: Double BOS Tokens
sections.summary: Explains that using apply_chat_template plus manually adding a BOS token creates double BOS tokens, which ruins finetuning by making inference accuracy lower since the model template becomes incorrect. Unsloth automatically removes the extra BOS token. This affects other models like Mistral and Gemma too.

sections.title: Llama 3 Bug 2: Untrained Tokens and Base Model
sections.summary: Untrained tokens (reserve special 0-250, end-of-turn, header tokens) in Llama 3 base cause NaN gradients. The instruct chat template must not be used with the base model. Fix by setting untrained tokens to mean of trained tokens, carefully masking untrained tokens when computing the average. Alternatively, train the LM head and embed tokens.

sections.title: Llama 3 Bug 3: Pad/EOS Token Conflict
sections.summary: If pad and EOS tokens are the same, pad masking during cross-entropy loss masks out the EOS token, causing infinite generations. Unsloth fixes this by selecting an untrained token or adding a new pad token with extra hashes. Phi-3 has this same issue.

sections.title: Ollama Export and Community Contributions
sections.summary: Covers automatic Ollama model file generation during finetuning with Colab notebooks for Alpaca and CSV datasets. Community contributions: CPU-only GGUF conversion due to float16 precision differences, llama.cpp now warns about double BOS tokens, and adding a system prompt can improve finetuning.

sections.title: Unsloth Features and Performance
sections.summary: Details Unsloth's GitHub package with automatic bug fixes, continued pre-training support with 5-10x reduced learning rate for LM head and embed tokens, 4x longer context via gradient offloading to system RAM (1-2% slower), and warnings against disk offloading and blocking calls.

sections.title: Colab Notebook Demo and LoRA Configuration
sections.summary: Live demo of Unsloth Colab notebook for Ollama finetuning showing installation, max sequence length, 4-bit training toggle, and model selection. LoRA configuration: rank 16 suggested (16-128, max equals model dimension), alpha should be rank times two, target all linear layers (QKV, down, up, gate) for optimal results, and use_rslora for automatic settings.

sections.title: Data Preparation and Chat Templates
sections.summary: Demonstrates Titanic CSV dataset fine-tuning. Ollama only supports two columns (instruction and output), so extra columns must be merged. Customizable chat templates now supported; must include two iterations due to dangling newlines or it errors out. Llama 3 chat template examples shown using Unsloth methodology.

sections.title: Training Methodology and Saving
sections.summary: Recommends batch size 2, gradient accumulation 4 (effective batch size 8), learning rate 2e-4 or smaller. Memory usage depends on batch size, not gradient accumulation. Inference uses apply_chat_template with Unsloth's double BOS fix. Saving now supports multiple GGUF files automatically without the previous 10-minute wait. Ollama model files are auto-generated. Links shared: tinyurl.com/unsloth2 for Ollama notebook, tinyurl.com/unsloth for workshop slides, plus Discord channel.
